messages:
sasha: Heads up — noticed a big LCP + main-thread spike on the console dashboards after the 11:30 canary (ekko-7) rollout. Sparklines freeze for ~1.5-2s when lots of series render. screenshot + perf logs attached :eyes:

james: saw it too. LCP went from ~2.1s -> ~4.9s on canary users. Trace shows main thread stuck on a function called `normalizeSeriesForRender` and a huge eval of a vendor chunk.

maya: likely a bundle/regression. Any chance a new chart transform landed? I remember ekko-7 added an optional data-wrangler to compute percentiles client-side.

sasha: yeah that matches. stack snippet from devtools: 
```
normalizeSeriesForRender (bundle.js:24321)
computePercentiles (vendor.chunk.js:112233)
Sparkline.render (sparkline.jsx:78)
```

carol: deploy-bot shows canary: ekko-7 -> 11:30, 450 users. rollback available. @eng-oncall any preference?

luis: quick bundle-scan shows vendor.chunk jumped +380KB, most of that is a new dependency: lightweight-stats (was supposed to be tree-shaken but got pulled into vendor).

james: we probably ship the percentile calc in the render path. Two quick mitigations: 1) defer percentile work to a webworker, 2) compute a cached downsample on the server / prefix cache. Both require short followups.

maya: simple hotfix: lazy-load the percentile code so initial paint doesn't wait. e.g. 
```
const compute = () => import('lightweight-stats');
useEffect(() => { compute().then(lib => lib.percentiles(...)); }, []);
```
That will keep sparkline paint fast for first frame.

sasha: +1 for lazy-load. Also telemetry: we need a custom trace/span tag to see which charts hit the heavy path. Right now our frontend traces just show bundletime.

james: agree. I'll add a span around `computePercentiles` and emit telemetry labeled `chart_variant: sparkline_v2`. That will let Optimize/Console correlate regressions to rollout flags.

carol: ops question — do we rollback canary for stability or push hotfix? Current error rate is low, but user-facing jank is high. @deploy-bot do we have an easy rollback?

deploy-bot: canary ekko-7 has rollback action: `/deploy rollback ekko-7 --canary`

luis: hotfix path looks straightforward — remove direct import and lazy-load, patch CDN build, promote. If we rollback, we'll lose other fixes in ekko-7. My vote: hotfix + canary monitor.

maya: also add a per-route bundle budget in our CI bundlestats check so big vendor pulls fail PRs. This slipped because package was optional dev-dep before.

sasha: action items summarized: 
- james: add telemetry span + deploy to canary (10m monitor)
- maya: open hotfix PR to lazy-load percentile lib and add webworker ticket if we need better perf
- luis: run bundle analyzer and revert bundling rules that pulled lightweight-stats into vendor
- carol: hold rollback if canary monitor shows improvement, otherwise roll back at 12:15.

james: starting the telemetry patch now. I'll ping when canary metrics show change :mag_right:

sasha: thanks — tagging @product so they know dashboard UX is impacted.

carol: noted. keeping an eye on alerts. :thumbsup:
